- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to underestimate late-period prices (last 5–7 days of forecast) — adjust downward bias by +2–3% for the final 10 days.  
- Overshoots after strong sentiment spikes (e.g., >0.7) often occur in day 10–15 of forecast — cap upward revisions at +5% of prior peak.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast shows 3+ consecutive downward drift, add 1–2% upward correction to prevent premature bottoming.  
- Sentiment volatility >0.35 in last 3 days correlates with forecast lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +1–2% to account for sentiment momentum.
